hlni.insight: A single task or module title is insufficient evidence to identify a degree category.
hlni.audienceGap: Students often assume that seeing one subject (like 'Revenue Analysis') proves a degree is B.Com or BBA.
hlni.viewerChange: Moves the viewer from making baseless guesses to asking for concrete, verifiable evidence (like official curriculum documentation).
hlni.support: Logical reasoning: In the absence of a verified source linking an example to a curriculum, a classification is logically impossible.
hlni.payoff: Shifts the burden of proof from the student's intuition to the student's ability to locate actual evidence.

candidate.reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: The Missing Link
candidate.creativeAngle: A logical reveal exposing the fallacy of guessing degrees from isolated, incomplete data points.
candidate.objective: Teach students to identify when they lack sufficient information to make a valid degree comparison.
candidate.targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Setup
shots.visual: A student stares at a whiteboard with the words 'Revenue Analysis' written clearly in marker.
shots.dialogue: Everyone wants to know: Is this a B.Com or BBA class?
shots.onscreenText: Is this B.Com or BBA? (Hint: It is neither.)
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the student's confused face.

shots.name: The Pivot
shots.visual: The student turns to the camera, shrugging while pointing at the board.
shots.dialogue: You can't tell. A single topic doesn't define a whole degree. You're guessing.
shots.cameraPerformance: Handheld, slightly shaky to imply urgency.

shots.name: The Method
shots.visual: The student holds up a blank sheet of paper and a pen.
shots.dialogue: Stop guessing. What specific document would prove which degree this belongs to?
shots.onscreenText: What specific document would prove which degree this belongs to?

productionNotes.sound: Clean room tone with a subtle 'pop' sound effect on text reveals.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Demonstrate that isolated examples are insufficient for classification and prompt the student to ask for verifiable source documentation.
shootingPriority: The direct question to the viewer

selected.title: The Missing Link
selected.audienceGap: Students assume a single example or course title automatically identifies the degree type.
selected.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
selected.viewerChange: Recognizes the danger of making assumptions based on incomplete data.
selected.concept: A 'reveal' where a single image of a lecture hall provides insufficient evidence to identify the degree.
selected.device: A riddle-style presentation showing one element and asking the viewer to 'guess' the degree, followed by the reveal that it's impossible.
selected.support: This is a reasoning limit: absent information cannot establish an exclusive classification.
methodSteps: Present one example without a source linking it to a category.
Separate a plausible guess from what the available information proves.
Identify the exact missing source or information needed to decide.
selected.interpretationRule: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.visibleProof: A forced-choice guess is replaced by a justified third answer and a precise request for missing evidence.
selected.payoff: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.limitations: Do not assert that the example belongs to both degrees, or to either one, without actual curriculum evidence.

demonstration.visibleInput: Is this B.Com or BBA? (Hint: It is neither.)
demonstration.observation: Viewer realizes the information is insufficient for a classification.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific document would prove which degree this belongs to?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: Split-screen comparison of two project prompts showing how different grading criteria change the focus of the task.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: A handwritten log where a student tracks a moment of confusion and turns it into a targeted question.
